alignments.note: Waw rendered *For* (rule 14, open connective list read off the ASV).

`מָה` is the predicate of this verbless clause and the definite construct chain `חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמָּעַל` is its subject, so the single written copula belongs to the interrogative, exactly as rule 20 gives the *is* of `מִי הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה` → *What man is this* to `מִי`. Headed on *what*, the word carrying the lexeme (rule 24). Corrected: the *is* had been attached to `חֵלֶק`. The competing reading takes `מֶה חֵלֶק` attributively, as the margin does, and is set aside under rule 38.
Construct noun with the supplied *the*, no article morpheme being present (rule 29). This noun heads the clause's subject, so the copula is not its; rule 20 sends it to the predicate `מָה`.
Nomen rectum takes the recast construct relation *from*, headed on the noun (rules 19, 24).
Preposition plus adverb rendered by one English word, the one-rendering condition being met; headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme (rules 30, 23).
Construct noun with the supplied *the* (rule 29). The interrogative is gapped in this line and the ASV writes no second copula, so there is nothing further to place.
Rectum takes the relational *from* and the determiner the ASV writes before its own word (rules 19, 29).

review_notes: Corrected one edge: the copula *is* (t003) was moved from `חֵלֶק` to `מָה`. `מָה` is the predicate of this verbless clause and the definite construct chain `חֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמָּעַל` is its subject, so rule 20's ruling on `מִי הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה` places the copula on the interrogative; the accepted reading had treated `חֵלֶק` as the predicate. Everything else is unchanged.

The ASV margin ("Or, For what portion should I have of God . . . And what heritage etc.?") was read and set aside under rule 38. That margin reads `מֶה חֵלֶק` attributively, as *what portion*; the printed text writes a copula between *what* and *the portion*, which is the division the alignment follows. The attributive reading is the competing one under rule 8.

After this correction JOB.31.2 and JOB.31.3 agree: the interrogative morpheme carries the clause's single written copula in both, `מָה` as the predicate here and `הֲ` as the fronted question auxiliary there.
The second line gaps the interrogative and writes no copula, so there is nothing to place on `נַחֲלַת`.
